column2: Ground improvement is the artificial improvement of the properties of the soils below the foundation that are dangerous in terms of settlement – by introducing foreign material and/or by compacting the soil. Four mechanical methods are presented below.

Dashed: the original strip footing of width b and contact pressure q; coloured: the modified one. On the left, the stress bulb (where σz is 20 % of the footing's own contact pressure); on the right, the vertical stress σz on the axis of the footing – calculated for an elastic half-space, with depth in units of b. The depth of the effect is set by the width of the foundation, the magnitude of the stress by the contact pressure.
